title: bn254-gt-dlp: gated tag-walk rho (a walk step is an inner product on 64-bit words with a two-tier certificate), 5 multipliers, window 3,500, expected work

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and z=g^x in the protected BN254 target group GT, the algorithm in proof.md recovers x (for z=1: x=0) with success at least 0.39, as algorithmic probability over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, under the disclosed heuristics H1 (an opened run, executed with all its caps, makes at most 107/100 times sqrt(pi r m/(2(m-1))) walk steps in expectation, m=5) and H2 (averaged rates over an opened run executed with its caps: the expected numbers of steps whose first tag, and whose second tag, is not certified are at most E_steps/26 and E_steps/2^50, and the expected number of reports is at most E_steps/2^89, against proved band shares 0.036621..., below 2^-54.7 and below 2^-90; the selector coordinate's exact p^2-Frobenius invariance and the steps that repeat earlier values are disclosed in proof.md section 7), supported by a proved tag lemma, algebra on the pinned constants and full-algorithm toy runs with a store keyed by the whole element. Before any other work the algorithm reads one fresh 64-bit coin u and opens the run only when u < K, K = 7203029819100908579, the least integer for which the opened share of runs times the supported success of an opened run reaches 0.39; a closed run costs 64 instructions and is counted as a failure. An opened run finds x by a sequential distinguished-point Pollard rho walk in GT with 5 multipliers g^c z^d: the next multiplier is read from one stored coordinate of the current element, a step computes a 64-bit tag as the inner product of 60 stored 51-bit digits with 60 table words and uses it only when the tag certifies the exact selector, and otherwise a second tag that adds the high halves of the products of the digits with 60 further table words and is exact to within 120 (proof.md section 2), the table holds every product of at most 3,500 multipliers, one Fp12 product re-bases the element every 3,500 steps, uncertified elements are evaluated exactly, distinguished elements (90 bits) go to an ordered store keyed by the whole element, and g^x=z is checked before output; it continues until it finds x or a counter reaches its cap. The score is an expectation: the expected total computation over the same uniform challenges and fresh coins is at most 2^118.738877 target-group-operation equivalents (scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C=20,000). It is not a bound on every run: on every run the total computation is at most 2^133.306392 equivalents, enforced by counters and the table structure (at most 3,501 trips per call of the step loop, because every child entry holds one more multiplier and entries of 3,500 multipliers have no children, a 3-word exit counter compared with its cap at every exit, 2^50 walk starts, 2^50 reports, 16 recoveries). Prices are executed instruction counts of generated AArch64 programs: 117 instructions per walk step (20 of the 60 digits held in registers for a whole call), 175 more per second tag, and 15,132 per exit from the step loop (one Fp12 product of 13,843 with the label additions, digits and counters, plus a stated allowance). Both totals include the gate, all input checks, constants, the table construction, fresh coins (16 instructions per 64-bit word), walk starts, reports, store operations, recoveries, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^62.604279 bytes in one address space with 64-bit pointers; preprocessing is at most 2^57.677273 equivalents and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Nothing is amortised over other targets, and no prior acceptance, submission or score is a premise. Analytic exploratory claim: no production-size run, not a finite-field sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Generate and execute the priced AArch64 programs (Fp multiply/add/sub, Fp12 product, the walk's step loop on real windows, the re-base with its counters on both sides of both caps, both sides of the certificate threshold, the trip budget) against big-integer arithmetic and print executed counts; check the tag lemma and the certified-selector corollary on production-size values; recompute every ledger integer, the gate constant K (and that K - 1 fails), the expected and every-run totals and the score; run the complete algorithm of proof.md to its output in the BN-family toy field q=p(-15), r'=r(-15). Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
